chunks: Abu Kurayb and Abu Saʿīd al-Ashajj narrated to me; they said: ʿAbdullah ibn Idrīs narrated to us, from his father Idrīs ibn ʿAbdullah al-Awdī, who said:

When al-Husayn (عليه السلام) was killed, the people wanted the horses to trample him. So Fiḍḍah said to Zaynab: “O my lady, Safīnah was once shipwrecked at sea and came out to an island, where he encountered a lion. He said: ‘O Abā al-Ḥārith, I am the mawlā of the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله).’ So it murmured before him until it stopped him on the road, while the lion remained crouching to one side. So let me go to it and inform it of what they intend to do tomorrow.”

He said: She went to it and said, “O Abā al-Ḥārith.” So it raised its head. Then she said, “Do you know what they intend to do tomorrow with Abū ʿAbdillah (عليه السلام)? They intend to have horses trample his back.” He said: So it walked until it placed its paws upon the body of al-Husayn (عليه السلام). Then the horses approached, but when they saw it, ʿUmar ibn Saʿd, may Allah curse him, said to them: “It is a disturbance; do not provoke it. Turn back.” So they turned back.

key_terms.أَبَا الْحَارِثِ: kunyah used in addressing the lion
key_terms.أَسَدٍ: a lion, which comes to guard the body
key_terms.الْحُسَيْنُ: al-Husayn (عليه السلام), the martyred Imam at the center of the report
key_terms.زَيْنَبَ: Zaynab, addressed by Fiḍḍah as her lady
key_terms.فِتْنَةٌ: a disturbance or turmoil, as described by ʿUmar ibn Saʿd
key_terms.فِضَّةُ: Fiḍḍah, who speaks to Zaynab and goes to the lion

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe the protection of the body of al-Husayn (عليه السلام) after Karbala?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates an episode after the martyrdom of al-Husayn (عليه السلام), when the enemy intended to have horses trample his blessed body. It relates that Fiḍḍah informed a lion, which then came and guarded the body, causing the assailants to withdraw. The report highlights the sanctity of al-Husayn (عليه السلام) and the gravity of the oppression committed at Karbala.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad said, ‘Abu Kureyb and Abu Saeed Al Ashajja narrated to me saying, ‘Abdullah Bin Idrees narrated to us, from his father Idrees Bin Abdullah Al Awdy who said,

‘When Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> was killed, the people (army) wanted the cavalry horses to trample him<sup>asws</sup>. So Fizza<sup>as</sup> said to (Syeda) Zaynab<sup>as</sup>: ‘O my<sup>as</sup> chieftess!’ A ship broke in the sea, so it came out to an island, and there he was with a lion. So he said, ‘O Abu Haris! I am a slave of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>!’ So it murmured to him until he paused upon the road, and the lion was crouching nearby. So leave me<sup>as</sup> to go to it and let it know what they are thinking of doing tomorrow’.

So he (the narrator) said, ‘So she<sup>as</sup> went to it and said: ‘O Abu Al-Haris!’ So it raised its head. Then she<sup>as</sup> said: ‘Do you know what they are intending of doing tomorrow with Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>? They are intending that the cavalry horses trample upon his<sup>asws</sup> back’. So it went until it placed its paws upon the body of Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup>. So the cavalry horses came over, but when they looked at it, Umar Bin Sa’d, may Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Curse him, said to them, ‘A strife! Do not raise it. Leave!’ So they left’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ahmad ibn Muhammad has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Hassan from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa ibn ‘Ubayd from Ali ibn Asbat from Sayf ibn ‘Amira from Muhammad ibn humran who has said the following.

“Abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) has said, ‘When all that happened to al-Husayn had happened, the angels wept and cried before Allah and said, “How such thing would happen to al-Husayn Your chosen one and the grand son of Your Prophet?” The Imam (a.s.) has said that Allah then showed to them the shadow of Al-Qa’im (the one who will rise with Divine Authority) and said, “Through him I will take My revenge.”
